title: Does equal-numbers stratified auditing still match the optimal split when the coder errs more in the rare group?
summary: On 3,188 real GoEmotions comments, the rare group is the longest 10.8% (344 comments, 23 or more words) and the estimand is the gap in negative-emotion prevalence to the rest (+0.072). Two naive-Bayes coders (not LLMs) have extra errors injected in the rare group only, by flipping each of their labels there with probability 0, 0.1, 0.2 or 0.3. The oracle share of the audit for the rare group stayed between 0.53 and 0.56, and an audit of equal numbers per group gave intervals within 0.7% of the optimal split at every injected rate (200 items: 0.333 against 0.331 with no injection, 0.346 against 0.344 at 0.3). A random audit stayed 1.66 to 1.69 times as wide. Coverage of the 95% interval was 0.95 to 1.00 for stratified designs (0.90 to 1.00 for random) (400 draws per cell, so about ±0.02). Limits: the coder already errs on 42–43% of rare-group items before injection, so random flips cannot raise the error spread much (the error rate reaches 0.50 and then falls back); a coder whose errors are more structured than coin flips is untested. One corpus, one grouping, one seed; no LLM was called.
lede: does equal-numbers stratified auditing still match the optimal split when the coder errs more in the rare group? On 3,188 GoEmotions comments, injecting up to 30% extra label flips in the rarest 11% group moved the optimal audit share only from 0.53 to 0.56, and equal numbers stayed within 0.7% of optimal width. Not an LLM.
